2650.translation: To Department Manager Lee: I dey request your approval. I attach contract with new client, so abeg review am. I go appreciate reply before today end.

2651.translation: Person wey get quick nunchi fit sense the other person mood even without explanation.

2652.translation: For Korea, plenty importance dey for keeping person dignity before other people.

2653.translation: For Lunar New Year day, people bow to elders and collect money gifts.

2654.translation: To describe traditions wey people regularly follow, use present-tense verbs, often with words for custom or tradition.

2655.translation: People dey talk say eating rice-cake soup for New Year morning add one year to your age.

2656.translation: During Chuseok, people visit ancestors graves.

2657.translation: Custom dey to chop seaweed soup for morning of person birthday.

2658.translation: For baby first birthday, dem hold party and let baby choose object from table.

2659.translation: Before winter reach, neighbours gather make kimchi together.

2660.translation: When person go wedding, e polite to give money gift for congratulations.

2661.translation: For funeral, people give condolence money and mourn quietly.

2662.translation: After moving to new house, people invite friends for housewarming party.

2663.translation: People dey remove shoes when dem enter house.

2664.translation: When drinking with elder, e polite to turn head away as you drink.

2665.translation: When giving something to elder, person dey use both hands.

2666.translation: Asking person wey you no know about age fit help decide how to address the person and which speech style to use.

2667.translation: For Korean, people often use our even for things like my house or my mama.

2668.translation: Ondol na traditional heating system wey dey warm floor.

2669.translation: People dey wear hanbok for special days, like holidays and weddings.

2670.translation: People believe say eating red-bean porridge for winter solstice fit drive bad luck away.

2671.translation: For hottest summer days, people dey chop ginseng chicken soup to regain strength.

2672.translation: For first full moon of year, people crack nuts and wish for healthy year.

2673.translation: For university entrance-exam day, offices dey start later and everybody dey encourage candidates.

2674.translation: For Korea, wey respect for parents important, plenty households dey live with parents and care for dem before.

2675.translation: Pumasi na tradition wey people help each other with work and return the favour.

2676.translation: For major holidays, families gather and hold ceremonies to remember ancestors.

2677.translation: For Hangul Day, people remember how King Sejong create Korean alphabet.

2678.translation: For jjimjilbang, people sweat and spend time with family and friends.

2679.translation: For meals, you begin chop after the oldest person pick spoon and chopsticks.

2680.translation: For long time, Korea get jeong culture of sharing food with neighbours.

2681.translation: One analysis say Korea ppalli-ppalli culture of doing things quickly take root during fast economic growth.

2682.translation: Choosing respectful or casual speech differently na language habit wey show your relationship with the other person.

2683.translation: For Korea, people often address person by job title or relationship, like somebody mama, instead of name.

2684.translation: Refusing offered food once or twice fit sometimes be person way of showing politeness.

2685.translation: Korean holiday culture dey change small-small. Before, family and relatives gather for one house and spend days preparing food and ancestral ceremonies. Now, more households prepare simple table or travel. Even when form change, spending time together and checking on each other still matter.

2686.translation: Intangible cultural heritage na knowledge and skills wey community members pass from one generation to another.

2687.translation: Even if its form change with time, traditional ceremony still fit strengthen community bonds.

2688.translation: Folk songs wey different regions pass down dey reflect local people lives and feelings.

2689.translation: To reduce cultural misunderstanding, we need avoid judging another culture only with our own standards.

2690.translation: People dey discuss respect for immigrants cultural identity as condition for bringing society together.

2691.translation: Today, we go look at preserving hanok from cultural-heritage policy angle. Hanok no be only place to live; na cultural creation wey reflect climate and way of life. But changing am for modern convenience fit damage its special structure. So balancing preservation with use na the main issue.

2692.translation: A: People criticise local festivals say dem too commercial. B: Because dem use visitor number judge success, stories wey special to the area don weaken in some ways. C: I see am differently. Residents need income to continue festival, so e hard to oppose all business activity itself. Wetin matter na system wey bring the income back to the local community.

2693.translation: Foundation announce results for traditional-craft preservation support. This year, dem choose seven out of thirty groups wey apply. Review focus on whether dem fit pass skills to next generation and their ties with local community. Groups wey dem no choose go receive written review comments.

2694.translation: A: People worry say dialects dey disappear. Wetin you think cause am? B: Standard language don spread through broadcasting and education. Also, young people move to cities, so chances to use dialect reduce. A: Wetin we should do to preserve dialects? B: No stop at recording dem. Link dem with local education so people go actually use dem for daily life.

2695.translation: Today lecture na about cultural context for translation. Word-for-word translation fit stay close to original, but some meanings fit still feel strange to readers. Free translation easy to read, but e fit erase the original special character. We go use examples compare both methods strengths and weaknesses.

2696.translation: A: Debate plenty about asking age first when people meet. How you see am? B: Korean address words and speech style depend on the other person. So asking age na practical way to set how conversation go run. C: I accept that use. But e no dey strengthen system wey older person control conversation? B: I no deny that side effect. But na result of the custom, no be why the custom first start. If address system change, the age question go naturally reduce too.

2697.translation: A: How we fit explain exchanging holiday gifts and making sure to return gifts? B: I see am as sign of long-term trust. Wanting return wetin person receive dey tie relationship together. C: But if people return exactly wetin dem receive, how e different from transaction? B: Outside, e fit look so. But for transaction, relationship end once payment complete. Deliberately adding small extra to return gift, so something still remain to return, show say person no intend end relationship. I no deny calculation. But the calculation aim na continuation, no be settling accounts.

2698.translation: A: Some people say everyday hanbok, wey dem adapt for daily wear, dey damage tradition. C: If dem no keep structure, like jacket-skirt proportion and ribbon ties, e hard to call am hanbok. B: I agree say basic structure matter. But if we insist on old material, length and fastening method too, nobody fit remain to wear am. C: You mean say if nobody wear am, tradition go stop. B: Yes. Cloth for museum and cloth wey people wear get different ways of preservation. I think the second one go last longer.

2699.translation: A: Fewer households dey live with parents. Awareness of care and respect for parents don weaken? B: I think say na form of expression change, no be only weakening. Even without living together, people fit share hospital bills and keep contact. C: That reading assume say family must continue carry care responsibility. That assumption itself no be the problem? B: The question valid. But until public system give enough support, we no fit remove that assumption overnight. Na after system dey in place we fit discuss care for parents as choice instead of obligation.
